answer: For every claimed identity, the verifier binds a fresh challenge—cedar, ledge, or ferrous—and requires a valid Wesolowski proof of a prescribed chain of modular squarings. The squarings within one chain are sequential, so GPUs cannot shorten that identity’s elapsed computation; clones may run concurrently, but each needs its own chain and resources. Sybil creation therefore faces a real time-and-computation bottleneck, not an impossible-to-parallelize workload across all identities.
